answer: A new identity must dock at a public jetty and post a non-transferable sable bond before it can transact. Admission then requires crossing a sequential bridge of four already-established, non-adjacent operators, each of whom assigns a unique unpaid audit and countersigns only original work. If two applicants share an operator key, their jetty records collide and both sable bonds are slashed. Until the full bridge is signed, rewards stay locked, so a farm cannot mint many full shares from one wallet.
